A particle executes simple harmonic motion according to the equation:
\(x=A\sin(\omega t+\phi_0).\)
At \(t=0,\) its displacement is \(x=\dfrac {A}{2,}\) and it is moving in the negative \(x \text-\)-direction. If \(0\leq \phi_0 \leq 2\pi,\) the initial phase angle \(\phi_0\) is:
1. \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\)

2. \(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\)

3. \(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\)

4. \(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(x=A\sin(\omega t+\phi_0), v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} =A\omega\cos(\omega t+\phi_0)\) Step: Find the initial phase angle\(\phi_0\). The equation of the SHM is given by; \(x=A\sin(\omega t+\phi_0)\) At \(t=0\), the displacement is \(y = \dfrac{A}{2}\)​, and the particle is moving along the negative \(x\text-\)direction then we get; \(\dfrac{A}{2} = A\sin(\phi_0)\) \(\Rightarrow \sin\phi_0 = \dfrac{1}{2}\) \(\Rightarrow \phi_0 = \sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2} \) \(\Rightarrow \phi_0 = \dfrac{\pi}{6}~\text{or}~\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\) The velocity of the particle is given by; \(v= \dfrac{dx}{dt} =A\omega \cos(\omega t + \phi_0 )\) At\(t=0\), the velocity of the particle is given by; \(v = A\omega \cos\phi_0\) As the particle is moving along the negative \(x\text-\)direction, so \(v<0.\) \(\cos\phi_0 <0 \) Therefore, the initial phase angle is\(\dfrac{5\pi }{6}.\) Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.
